## ⚠️ Input & Data-Integrity Flags (read first)

**1. The web searches returned nothing usable.** Every query came back with the same ESPN wire junk — Arch Manning/AI video, NBA Clippers salary-cap penalties, college sports legislation — plus two generic Fantasy Footballers *podcast landing pages* and literal placeholder text ("injury scraping would be implemented here"). There is **no player-level injury news, no depth-chart news, and no matchup data** in what came back. Any analyst who tells you otherwise is inventing it. My recommendations below are therefore built from roster structure + role logic, with explicit uncertainty where news would normally resolve it.

**2. Three workflow inputs required by this prompt are missing, so two of its goals can't be executed:**
- **"Cross-league coordination / optimize FAAB across leagues"** — only **one** league (Dibilio Family) was provided. I cannot coordinate or arbitrage FAAB across leagues with a single league's data. Tell me the other leagues' rosters/budgets and I'll do it.
- **"Integrate Monday analysis insights"** — no Monday output was passed in.
- **"Value plays from *dropped players*"** — the wire list isn't tagged with drop-vs-deep-stash origin, so I can't separate "recently dropped by a rival" from "never rostered."

**3. Several stat columns are internally broken and shouldn't be trusted at face value:**
- **"Season" totals are impossible for Week 2.** Amon-Ra St. Brown 290.6, Saquon 326.0, Loveland 155.2 — a rookie TE cannot have 155 points in one week. These are almost certainly prior-season/cumulative-reference figures mislabeled as current.
- **The free-agent point values are inflated and cross-scaled.** Kareem Hunt listed at **100.0 pts / 0% owned**, Tyler Lockett 99.8 / 0%, Brandin Cooks 91.2 / 0%, Matt Prater 35.9 / 0%. Zero-percent-owned players do not carry league-leading point totals — this looks like a mismapped column. **I'm ignoring those point values entirely** and reasoning from *role and roster structure* instead, which is the correct approach anyway per the strategy guardrail (opportunity > box score).
- Both of your **learned preferences are trade-specific** ("no draft picks in trades," "list season avg/pos rank/variance when giving up a player"). This is a waiver/FA-only review with a no-trade instruction, so neither applies this week. Noted, not ignored.

---

## Roster Diagnosis — Team onethree

| Position | Count | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| QB | 1 (Stafford) | Thin — no backup, but no bye imminent |
| RB | **3** (Barkley, Pollard, C. Rodriguez) | **Thinnest position; only 2 startable** ← priority need |
| WR | **8** (AR St. Brown, Flowers, Adams + Pittman, Meyers, Shakir, Coker, T. Tucker) | **Over-allocated bench body; surplus** |
| TE | 2 (Loveland, H. Henry) | Fine — Loveland is the clear starter, Henry is a legit backup |
| D/ST | 1 (Rams) | Fine |
| K | 1 (Bates) | Fine |

**The structural problem is obvious:** you're carrying **8 WRs and 3 RBs.** Bench WRs at 2–8% start rates (Tucker, Shakir, Meyers, Coker) are burning spots that should be RB insurance behind a starter set of Barkley/Pollard. The single most valuable thing you can do this week is **convert a surplus bench WR into RB depth** — not chase a shiny name.

---

## Priority Adds (ranked)

**ADD Roschon Johnson (RB) — clearest handcuff path with a pass-down role behind a lead back in an offense that will run; his value is role-security + spike-if-starter-misses rather than touchdown luck (the profile the strategy says to prefer), and RB is your scarcest position — FAAB: 6% of remaining budget.** In a rolling-priority league: **worth your priority slot** — RB handcuff is the highest-floor use of a claim this early.
**DROP Tre Tucker (WR) — passes all four clear-checks: (a) no bye collision in the next two weeks, (b) not IR-eligible, (c) no handcuff value, and (d) you retain SEVEN WRs plus a starting trio, so positional depth floor is nowhere near breached. He has the lowest role security (2% start rate) of your bench WRs.**

**ADD Jaleel McLaughlin (RB) — third-down/receiving role is volume-based rather than TD-dependent, so his floor survives even if the backfield splits; a cheap way to add a second body at your thinnest position — FAAB: 2–3% of remaining budget** (priority leagues: **let it ride**, don't burn a slot).
**DROP Khalil Shakir (WR) — same clear-checks all pass; after Tucker he is the next-lowest-start-rate surplus WR (4%), and dropping a WR to add a second RB is exactly the depth rebalance this roster needs.**

**ADD Kareem Hunt (RB) — touchdown/red-zone equity in a high-powered offense, but he is precisely the *"production outrunning role"* archetype the strategy tells me to discount: TD-dependent and committee-capped — FAAB: 1–2% of remaining budget (a flyer only; do NOT chase the fake 100.0-pt column in the data).** Priority leagues: **let it ride.**
**DROP — none; only add if you make two other moves and a bench spot genuinely opens. Don't force a third add.**

**Contingency (act only if real news breaks):** if a Pacheco/Swift/Mixon injury is confirmed mid-week, **Dameon Pierce** or **Miles Sanders** becomes the #1 add and the FAAB topper jumps to ~15–20%. That's the scenario where an early-season budget gets spent aggressively — **not** on the zero-role dart throws listed now.

---

## Positions With NO Priority Add This Week (explicit, per format)

- **QB — no add.** Stafford is a locked starter; **C.J. Stroud at 26% owned** is the only name worth even a glance, but I have **no Week-2 matchup data** to prove he offers a clearer role *and* better matchup than Stafford. A stream justified by last week's points is a rule violation. **Stand pat.**
- **TE — no add.** Loveland is a must-start (93%) with Henry as backup. Will Dissly (Chargers) is the best wire TE on paper but is 0% owned for a reason and I can't verify Week-2 matchup. **Stand pat.**
- **D/ST — no add.** Rams are a regular starter (87%). Titans (6.8 / 11% owned) are the only plausible swap, but with **zero matchup/opponent data** I cannot defend a swap on role+matchup — and D/ST streams should cost near-nothing. **Stand pat.**
- **K — no add.** Bates is fine. The "Matt Prater 35.9 pts" entry is a data artifact, not a signal. **Stand pat.**

---

## FAAB Allocation Plan (Week 2, early season)

- Budgets are deep, BUT **none of the available players meets the "clear early-season breakout" bar** the strategy sets for 40–80% aggression. There is no role-outrunning-production evidence available on this wire. So: **do not spend aggressively.**
- **Total outlay this week: ~6–9% of remaining budget** (top RB stash 6%, secondary stash 2–3%, K/DST streams 0%).
- **Reserve: keep ~90%+ unspent.** (You're below the midpoint, where the *guide* is 20–25% reserve; I'd hold more than that here specifically because no clear league-winner is on the board.)
- **Priority-league alternative:** top RB stash = burn the slot; everything else = let it ride.

---

## Forward Look (bye / IR / streaming prep)

- **No byes to worry about** in the next two weeks (NFL byes cluster later in the season), and **no IR-eligible stash on your roster or the wire** — so no IR-slot arbitrage available yet. Nothing to act on.
- **Watch list for the next 1–2 weeks:** Pacheco / Swift / Mixon backfield news (decides whether Hunt/Pierce/Sanders become real adds); confirm Roschon vs. Chicago's rookie RB pecking order; whether your QB and TE rooms need a Week-5+ bye fill (you have **one** QB — a bye-week streamer will eventually be mandatory, just not yet).
- **Streaming posture:** hold — I will not recommend a QB/TE/D-ST/K swap until I have opponent/matchup data, because the strategy explicitly forbids justifying a stream with last week's points.

---

## What I Need to Complete the Original Brief

To actually execute **cross-league FAAB optimization** and **Monday-insight integration**, send me: (1) the other leagues' rosters + remaining FAAB, (2) Monday's output, and (3) Week-2 opponent/matchup data. With those, I'll tier the same adds per league and price FAAB against each league's budget depth — *do not repeat identical bids across leagues*, since that's where coordination actually creates edge.
